result.title: Simple Baselines for Fetal Brain Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
result.comment: Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
result.summary: Unsupervised anomaly detection (UAD) offers a promising approach to fetal brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analysis, where pathological data are scarce. Existing methods rely mainly on brain age prediction or image reconstruction, but are limited by noisy gestational age (GA) labels, lack of lesion localization, or poor cross-domain generalization. We propose FetalBUAD, a UAD framework based on voxel-level brain age estimation. A joint multi-task network predicts global brain age, voxel-level brain age maps, and brain segmentation to establish an internal biological brain age reference, reducing reliance on clinically recorded GA. Uncertainty-aware voxel-level brain age gap maps are then used for anomaly localization. Experiments on 1,317 internal fetal brain MRI volumes and an external benchmark demonstrate state-of-the-art anomaly detection performance and improved cross-domain generalization. FetalBUAD also generates anatomically interpretable maps that localize diverse fetal brain abnormalities. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/birthlab/FetalBUAD.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 FetalBUAD，用多任务网络同时预测全局脑龄、体素级脑龄图与脑分割，以体素级脑龄差构建不确定性异常定位图，用于胎儿脑 MRI 的无监督异常检测。
